video_title: Head Coach Jordan Ott Practice Media Availability | 10-12-26

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on Miles Bridges' ankle recovery and playing status
quotes.excerpt: the ankle is recovering at a good rate, but that's the one where we're not going to press.
quotes.quote: The ankle is recovering at a good rate, but that's the one where we're not going to press. That's the one I'm talking about. We're not going to press on if it's not perfect.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says the Suns will not press on Miles Bridges' ankle recovery. The team is prioritizing caution, stating they are not going to push it if the injury is not perfect.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on the team's preparation for the upcoming season
quotes.excerpt: He knows how to prepare his self, his body and mind for what's about to come.
quotes.quote: He knows how to prepare his self, his body and mind for what's about to come. Marathons are about to come and he's had a great summer, but now it's a fine tuning as we get into the season.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says the team is in a period of fine tuning as they prepare for the long season ahead. He noted that the players have put in the work over the summer to get their bodies and minds ready.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on the unique shooting ability of Kevin Durant
quotes.excerpt: his ability to still move in today's league, I think that's different.
quotes.quote: His ability to still move in today's league, I think that's different. Joe Harrison and Kyle Korver did it in a different time period where now it's not as much. It's more like handoffs from a stationary five, before it was a little bit of dribble handoffs but it was a lot of pin downs. So that's a little bit different. He has a very quick release, incredible touch, and that's just one part of his game.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott breaks down what makes Kevin Durant unique, highlighting his quick release and incredible touch. He notes that Durant's movement in today's league is different from the shooters of previous eras.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on Kevin Durant's improved shot selection and confidence
quotes.excerpt: He's a confident shooter now, off the bounce and off the catch.
quotes.quote: He's a confident shooter now, off the bounce and off the catch. He's definitely improved. 12 months he's definitely improved. He was here all summer. A lot of times it was late at night with his brother coming back. He has his own people to come in. He knows that's a part of his game that he could get better at and he did.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says Kevin Durant has definitely improved his shooting off the bounce and off the catch over the last 12 months. He credited Durant's work ethic, noting he spent much of the summer training late at night.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on the importance of depth in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: If you just play some time in the NBA, you see how depth matters.
quotes.quote: If you just play some time in the NBA, you see how depth matters. You're going to get your opportunity. We saw it last year. You see it around all sports. It feels like the NFL has a ton of injuries. Everyone's going to get their opportunity. You got to be ready to play. And even though you could be out of the rotation to start, your name's going to be called, then it's are you ready? Are you ready and then can you do it at a high enough level time after time after time?
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott emphasizes the importance of depth in the NBA. He warns players that even if they are out of the rotation to start, their name will be called and they must be ready to perform at a high level.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on balancing player strengths with team system
quotes.excerpt: We don't want to change the player per se, like we want to highlight their greatest skills.
quotes.quote: We don't want to change the player per se, like we want to highlight their greatest skills within the framework of what we how we want to play and the identity of our group. It's a balance, but it's first and foremost learning your players, watching them from afar especially if they've had a career. And then even young guys coming into the system, they still have superpowers that can translate to the NBA.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on team philosophy: We don't want to change the player. We want to highlight their greatest skills within the framework of our identity.
